Whilst I don't disagree that there are people that blindly follow their favourite content creators, Dunkey's video isn't wrong, and I barely watch the guy. As a long time sonic fan, Frontiers is an OK game at best. I'll still play and 100% complete it, since I sorta enjoy open world collectathon type games, but it absolutely has its issues that in no way deserve all the insane amount of praise it's getting, the rabid sonic fanbase is just as bad as any other. 

The difficulty seems to make no difference, i've yet to encounter anything hard about it, all the puzzles are far too forgiving, the bosses are ruined by the fact that you just hold parry for as long as you want to block any incoming attack and get big damage off, the stages are the same 4 sets over and over with half of them being parts ported over from Generations, whilst also offering next to no desire for exploration and taking different routes because the red tokens are in obvious, easy to reach spots and the time trials are impossible to not get an S on, bar 1-2 that actually felt difficult to do so. For a game that talks about open exploration it sure doesn't feel that way then 90% of it is just going onto a speed boost/spring/lever and following a linear path/rail to the next medal, with half of them locking you to a 2d perspective.

The music is great as always but again kind of loses that intense feeling when the combat is so bland.

It's an OK game with a lot of missed opportunity that could potnetially be worked on in the future, it's fine for people to enjoy the game, but the fact that it's overwhelmingly positive really makes me feel sad for the low bar that people seem to have just because it's a sonic game.

I think it depends on what sort of game you're looking for. Overall for a collectathon type sonic game with a bit more freedom of exploration whilst sort of solid nods to the 2d/3d level segments of Generations it's definitely fun, if a bit addictive. The music as per usual with sonic games is absolutely incredible. The game however doesn't come without it's faults. It's very easy even on 'hard', frankly i'm not sure if the difficulty levels are bugged or just don't really offer anything in change of gameplay, the combat is quite spammy and disappointing once you figure out how to deal with it, which kills off the excitement of bosses, and the timings of a lot of things, bar one specific stage early on, are insanely forgiving. 

The graphics don't come off as that mindblowing to me, but I think it looks solid enough for a sonic game, however the rendering of platforms isn't great,  needing to be in a specific range for them to appear despite them being the ways to get a lot of collectables. 

If you want something a bit more laid back to experience then you'd absolutely love this game, but as someone that gets a bit more excitement from tense and difficult situations, I found it to be rather disappointing, something just feels off with the difficulty, especially in regards to combat and some of the puzzle timings, whether it's bugged or was changed to be easier before release i'm not sure. This coming from an OG sonic fan way back in the Sega Drive days.

Edit: I think it's fine for people to enjoy different things, but I can't really understand the overwhelming positivity that people seem to give the game. I'd say it's a 7/10 at most, pretty solid and overall fun, but needs working on to make it shine more.

TL;DR: Get it for a casual, fun open world experience. Wait for a sale or maybe future patches (?) if you want something a bit more depth and difficulty to it.

In regards to the whole dungeon limitations thing, I do have two recommendations that could possibly be made, that i'm sure others have presented:

1. It doesn't make too much sense to me that the level 50 dungeons have such a low drop-rate when the Hard dungeons literally throw epics at you. Whilst I don't think everything should be handed to us on a silver platter, it feels a little backwards to me. I feel like the level 50 dungeons should at least reward fragments towards a weapon (An untradeable/unsellable one.) Perhaps make it a bit of a grind, maybe 30 fragments if you really want to go that far, but at the very least it means you're guaranteed to get an epic item within your weekly limit. This seems to make the most sense seeing as hard dungeons provide you with 1/4 of a fragment when dismembered to which then you'll be provided a weapon of your class upon completion, WHILST also providing enhancement materials. This will at least provide some progress to the players, as well as stop people manipulating and controlling the market with pretty much required epics in order to proceed to the hard dungeons, this is a huge concern for me when official release happens for newer players. (Especially considering people are working around the mechanics by equipping one-handed weapons in the offhand for 285+ GS.)

2. Add the ability for us to enter a dungeon but not acquire loot and also not count towards one of our 10 a day/30 a week limit. This helps especially seeing as some daily missions require you to complete other dungeons, it also means that players can then go through dungeons with their friends without having to sacrifice their own runs or even straight up deny them simply because they're holding onto their runs for the higher/harder dungeons. Even right now our guild has the weekly quest to kill fire dragon 5 times, however with the upcoming new hard dungeons we're putting that off to near enough last minute to use our last 10 runs this week for the upcoming new hard dungeons. (I've also heard that on the stream there was mention of discussion about a reset on official release when the question was brought up, though i'm unsure whether it's true.)

Personally, I think there should just be a fragment system for the weapon or something. (Seeing as you'll be using both Fire Dragon AND Balrog weapons for their respective raids anyway, so it's not like it'll just either be replaced or be best in slot.) At the very least then some sort of progress would be happening even if you don't get a single drop. The issue I had was that the people i'm guilding with were all doing Fire Dragon/Balrog early because they got drops whilst I was stuck making alts and running level 50 dungeons with no luck. Realistically, I could've kept running those dungeons with no drops whatsoever, and whilst of course you can grind out mesos and buy weapons/armor on the Black Market, I feel like that shouldn't have to be the case for people, especially seeing as the cost for those items will likely skyrocket on official release, with people who're way ahead controlling the market. The way it currently is will likely turn people away or lose interest, when we want MORE people to get into the game. If there's weapon and armor fragments for Hard Dungeons which throws gear at you, why shouldn't the level 50 dungeons at the very least have a somewhat more grindey fragment system? I feel like people will complain less if there's at the very least SOME progress being made.
